title: Grateful Dead Live at RFK Stadium on 1973-06-10

ai_review.summary: A superb matrix mix captures a legendary 1973 show – from a soaring Morning Dew to an epic Dark Star with a monster Phil Lesh jam – sounding full, clear and immersive.
ai_review.review: The Kevin Tobin matrix does an outstanding job of blending the dry soundboard with ambient audience cues, delivering crisp clarity and depth that makes listeners feel right in the venue. Musically the concert is often hailed as one of the band's finest, highlighted by a powerful Dark Star, a jaw‑dropping Bird Song jam and a third set featuring Dickey Betts’s guest brilliance. While a couple of reviewers note occasional “cheesy” artifacts from mismatched sources, the consensus is that both performance and recording are top‑tier.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of detailed reviews (9/12) give 4–5 stars and praise both the show’s musical peaks and the matrix recording’s clarity; only a few low‑star comments focus on source mismatches, so overall quality is rated very good.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Matrix blend praised for adding ambience and depth while keeping the soundboard’s clarity; listeners describe it as crisp, full and ‘like you’re there’. A minority mention occasional cheesiness or muddy audience bleed where the SBD and AUD differ in quality.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert moves from a mellow, jazzy‑jammy first half into tight, high‑energy improvisations, culminating in a remarkable third set that many reviewers call epic.

band_member_comments.Jerry: His guitar work and interplay with Dickey Betts are highlighted; fans note his “Stellas” and trading jams as standout moments.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as delivering a “monster jam” on Dark Star, hailed as a rock‑and‑roll god in this performance.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum presence is noted for its clarity and spatial feel within the matrix mix.
